sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale International Distribution of Acetate Eyeglass Frames

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (national unitary jurisdiction; corporate register executed locally via the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the INPI Guichet Unique; no sub-state corporate registry distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code, as amended by EU-derived commercial law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 30 May 1984; entered into force 15 March 1985)
France–Hong Kong SAR Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 21 November 1995; entered into force 9 June 1997)
France–United States Double Taxation Avoidance Treaty (1967; amended by the 2006 Protocol)
EU–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (entered into force 1 February 2019)
EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (negotiations concluded 30 December 2020; not ratified, not in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L.561-1 to L.561-59 and R.561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT obligations); Article L.561-2-2 (beneficial-owner definition); Articles L.561-45 to L.561-49 (beneficial-owner declaration); Décret n°2016-731 of 1 June 2016; Arrêté of 24 June 2016 (UBO declaration content); Décret n°2023-497 of 21 June 2023 (transfer of UBO register to the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle, effective 1 August 2023); Code de commerce, Articles L.123-11-1 and R.123-9 et seq. (corporate domiciliation).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each shareholder and of the appointed gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary or competent certification authority in the country of origin of the shareholder or gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (France is party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; for documents issued in the People's Republic of China, Apostille under the PRC accession effective 7 November 2023; documents predating such accession require consular legalization via the French Consulate of jurisdiction)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of corporate register / Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., State Administration for Market Regulation in the PRC; Companies Registry in Hong Kong SAR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the designated Competent Authority of the issuing State, followed by certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing KYC standing of each corporate shareholder and source of the capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding banking institution of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the issuer or notarized certified copy with apostille where the receiving French bank requires formal authentication; otherwise accepted as sworn private deed under Article L.561-7 CMF client-file rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Latest annual financial statements, management accounts, or independent audit report of each corporate shareholder (capital provenance and traceability)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified public accountant / independent auditor of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the certified copy, followed by certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record / police clearance for the appointed gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal record authority of the country of nationality or of last residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, followed by certified French translation by an approved legal translator

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all identified shareholders, UBOs and the gérant against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions File; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the OFAC SDN and consolidated non-SDN lists under extraterritorial compliance practice; (iv) France's national asset-freezing and financial sanction lists published by the Direction générale du Trésor; and (v) PEP databases per the ACPR AML/CFT guidelines. Customer due diligence per Articles L.561-4-1, L.561-5, L.561-6 and R.561-10 et seq. CMF; enhanced due diligence and suspicious-activity reporting to TRACFIN per Articles L.561-10-2, L.561-15 and L.561-15-1 CMF. PEP status persists for 5 years after cessation of the public function (Article R.561-18-1 CMF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI); name availability search against the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) via data.inpi.fr; residual support through the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce having territorial jurisdiction
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in the French language. A foreign-language name is admissible only where it reflects an essential element of the company's commercial activity, but it must be rendered in Latin characters. Under the Loi Toubon (Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994), French-language wording is mandatory for the articles of association, commercial documents, invoicing and contracts executed on French territory; a certified French translation of any foreign-language annex is required.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Crédit / Finance / Capital (misleading financial-institution connotation restricted)
Avocat / Notaire / Expert-comptable / Huissier (regulated professions — ministerial register authorization required)
Pharmacie / Pharmacien / Opticien (regulated health-profession title protection)
État / République / National / Municipalité (false indication of public authority)
France Officielle / République Française / tricolor emblem (protected emblem and false-flag prohibition)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the guichet unique or by the greffe du tribunal de commerce, the founder may: (i) file a written administrative refutation with the same registry within 7 working days of the refusal notice, submitting prior-use evidence, trademark registration or trade-name usage proof; (ii) lodge a summary application (assignation en référé) before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce having territorial jurisdiction within 15 days of the refusal, whose decision is exclusive over RNCS insertion disputes; (iii) alternatively, file a French trademark application (marque) with the INPI to convert the name into a proprietary right and remove the registry's relative ground of refusal. The 28-day priority window is not automatically extendable; a fresh reservation must be filed while preserving the sequence among legal-announcement publication, articles drafting and RCS filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted subject to conditions. A SARL may domicile its registered office with an approved business-domiciliation company under Articles L.123-11-1 and R.123-9 et seq. of the French Code de commerce, provided a convention de domiciliation is executed, the domiciliation company is duly registered with the competent Chamber of Commerce, and the term of the convention does not exceed 9 years. For the wholesale international distribution of ophthalmic eyeglass frames (ISIC 4646), a virtual office is acceptable for administrative seat, mail handling and statutory address in France, but the entity must retain actual local administrative capacity and a verifiable document trail for customs clearance, contract archiving, invoice issuance and litigation service of process; the domiciliation address is published in the RCS and constitutes the statutory seat for all formal notifications.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting and review of Articles of Association (statuts) for a multi-member or single-member SARL, including quota allocation, gérant appointment and corporate governance clauses
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fee (EUR 1,500) per French National Bar incorporation drafting practice; notarial tariff applies only if the statuts are executed by acte notarié

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Guichet Unique formalities — RNCS name availability search and filing of corporate name reservation (avis de constitution)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory electronic formalities fee (EUR 40) per INPI tariff schedule effective for the guichet unique regime

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) in the jurisdiction of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated rate per line (average EUR 4.10 per line, statutory ceiling) for an 8-line announcement, total approximately EUR 220 in the Paris and major commercial jurisdictions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of apostilled identity, corporate good-standing and police-clearance documents (bilingual notarial fascicle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark rate of EUR 35 to EUR 45 per source page, with an estimated 6 to 8 pages per incorporation file

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille serialization of the mandatory document bundle (5 core documents) and international courier chain
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Authority of the issuing State (e.g., PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs; Hong Kong SAR Government Records Service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille tariff of approximately EUR 30 to EUR 50 per document, plus courier and administrative handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate domiciliation agreement (1-year term) with a registered business-domiciliation company in the planned registered-office jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark rate for a commercial wholesaler of approximately EUR 40 per month (annual EUR 480)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration filing — immatriculation of the SARL via the guichet unique, including payment of greffe costs and mandatory ancillary filings
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff (EUR 42) per the French tariffs applicable to the guichet unique (Code de commerce, Article R.123-33 and associated fee schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial-owner (UBO) register statement preparation and compliance verification against the 25% ownership threshold
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark professional fee of EUR 350, typically merged within the incorporation package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation AML/CFT screening of UBOs against EU, UN, OFAC and French national sanctions and PEP databases, including generation of the entity risk-assessment file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML/CFT data screening provider / compliance operator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark software license and query cost of approximately EUR 100 per entity file

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L223-1 to L223-43 and R223-1 to R223-36; Civil Code provisions on contracts and contributions; French Monetary and Financial Code provisions on beneficial-owner identification and anti-money-laundering controls.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The online Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the National Institute of Industrial Property (Institut national de la propriété industrielle, INPI), with registration in the Registre national des entreprises (RNE) and, for a commercial SARL, the relevant Commercial Court Registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce) and Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of company formation (déclaration de constitution) submitted through the Guichet unique, supported by the executed Articles of Association (statuts), publication notice, beneficial-owner declaration, and prescribed supporting documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to a SARL. The capital must be divided into quota shares. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Contributions are deposited into a blocked account with a bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations and released after registration. Contributions in kind must be described in the Articles; an auditor of contributions is generally required unless statutory waiver conditions are satisfied.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders, acting as the duly constituted corporate body of [Company Name] SARL, resolve to approve the Articles of Association and confirm subscription of the entire capital of EUR [amount], divided into [number] quota shares of EUR [nominal value] each, with cash contributions paid as legally required. The registered office is established at [full French address]. [Name] is appointed Manager (gérant) for an indefinite term, with authority to represent the Company within the limits of applicable law and the Articles. [Optional additional officer names and functions] are appointed effective immediately. The Manager is authorized to complete all registration and banking formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate structure, name, purpose, and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises; relevant Commercial Court Registry for local RCS processing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the SARL form, verify the proposed name through the INPI and trademark databases, define the corporate purpose for wholesale distribution of acetate ophthalmic frames, and secure a French registered office. Obtain a domiciliation agreement, commercial lease, or manager-owned premises declaration. Notarization is not normally required for ordinary Articles signed privately; notarization is required where a notarial asset contribution or real-estate transfer is involved.
required_dossiers: Manager identification and declaration of non-conviction and parentage
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
Certified French translations of foreign-language documents, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the Articles, address evidence, identification documents, translations, or ownership data through the Guichet unique query workflow. Resubmit within the stated cure period and retain the electronic filing receipt. Escalate unresolved registry issues to the relevant Commercial Court Registry or use the available INPI support and administrative challenge channels.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Depositary bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations; INPI Guichet unique for the subsequent filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the Articles and subscription schedule. Open a temporary capital account, transfer the required paid-in cash contribution, and obtain the deposit certificate. Ensure that the Articles identify capital, quota shares, contributions, manager, registered office, duration, and corporate purpose. Foreign shareholders should provide legalized or otherwise acceptable corporate extracts, signing authority evidence, and French translations where requested.
required_dossiers: Shareholder corporate extracts or identity documents
Contribution auditor report or waiver documentation, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify incomplete know-your-customer documentation, ownership evidence, or payment references. If a bank refuses the account, obtain written refusal and seek another eligible depositary or use the statutory deposit mechanism, subject to acceptance of the documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the required formation notice containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, manager identity, and applicable registration information. Obtain the attestation of publication or publication certificate for the Guichet unique filing. The notice must be published in an authorized JAL serving the registered-office department.
required_dossiers: JAL publication order and payment evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction or republication if the notice contains a material error, then upload the corrected attestation. A filing query caused by an invalid or incomplete notice should be cured before the registry deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic company-formation form, select commercial activity and SARL status, upload the Articles, publication attestation, deposit certificate, manager declarations, registered-office evidence, beneficial-owner filing, and foreign-document translations. Pay the applicable registry and beneficial-owner charges. Verify that the stated activity is wholesale distribution rather than manufacturing if the company will not fabricate or transform frames.
required_dossiers: Manager declaration of non-conviction and parentage
Foreign shareholder documents and certified translations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the electronic dashboard and respond to any INPI, RCS, tax, or beneficial-owner query. Upload corrected documents promptly, preserving consistent company data across all documents. If rejected, identify the specific legal deficiency, amend the filing or Articles, and resubmit; challenge a legally unsupported refusal before the competent registry or court where appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration evidence and activate governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant Commercial Court Registry and INPI RNE; business tax administration through the company registration process
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence, verify SIREN, SIRET, APE code, RCS details, manager identity, and registered office, and request release of deposited capital. Open the permanent operating bank account. Maintain the Articles, shareholder register, capital records, manager appointment record, beneficial-owner evidence, accounting records, and annual accounts timetable. Registration does not itself create an industrial manufacturing authorization.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Report factual errors to the Commercial Court Registry or INPI and submit an amendment filing. If the registered activity or address is incorrect, file the relevant modification before commencing the affected activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF, French tax administration, customs authority (DGDDI), and local authorities as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the manager and employees with the appropriate social-security systems, configure payroll and workplace insurance, confirm corporate-tax and VAT treatment, and obtain an EORI number if importing or exporting goods. Establish product traceability and conformity files for frames marketed in the European Union. Wholesale distribution alone generally requires no separate commercial operating license, but premises, signage, waste, fire, and customs obligations remain applicable.
required_dossiers: EORI application documents, if cross-border customs activity applies
Product invoices and supplier conformity records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct registration data with the relevant authority, file amended VAT or customs information, and suspend the affected activity until mandatory registrations or safety measures are complete. Retain evidence of submissions and authority acknowledgements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ordinary wholesale distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames. If the business later manufactures, coats, chemically treats, or materially transforms frames, the relevant prefecture and the regional environmental authority must assess authorization under the classified-installations regime (Installations classées pour la protection de l'environnement, ICPE).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific manufacturing or wholesale operating permit is ordinarily required for wholesale distribution of acetate eyeglass frames. Separate premises, customs, fire-safety, waste, and employment registrations may nevertheless apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: French Ministry for Ecological Transition, with the competent regional environmental authority (Mission régionale d'autorité environnementale, MRAe) and the relevant departmental prefecture where an environmental authorization or assessment is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for ordinary office and warehouse wholesale activity, provided no manufacturing, surface treatment, significant emissions, regulated waste treatment, or other listed ICPE activity is undertaken. A case-specific screening is required for substantial storage, chemical use, or industrial transformation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine industrial wastewater or VOC threshold applies to a pure wholesale operation. Any discharge must comply with the French Environmental Code and the local sewer authority's authorization and limits. Waste, packaging, hazardous substances, and contractor disposal must be segregated, documented, and transferred to authorized operators. Manufacturing or coating activities may trigger ICPE emission, wastewater, storage, and hazardous-waste requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain premises fire-risk assessment, compliant emergency exits, extinguishers, alarms, electrical inspection, evacuation signage, and employee safety documentation. An establishment open to the public may require approval under the Établissement recevant du public (ERP) rules from the competent municipality or prefecture. Warehouse structural load and racking safety must be verified by competent professionals where relevant. Occupational-risk assessment, workplace accident prevention, training, and the mandatory document unique d'évaluation des risques professionnels are required. No general pre-opening industrial clearance applies unless the premises or activity falls within ERP, ICPE, building, or workplace-specific regimes.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), operating through impots.gouv.fr and formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique/INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned SARL obtains its French tax identity as follows: (1) file constitution through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; (2) receive SIREN/SIRET numbers from INSEE; (3) register as an employer and tax payer with DGFIP; (4) apply for a French intra-Community VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) via DGFIP; non-European non-resident operators generally must appoint an accredited tax representative in France for VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. A SARL is by default subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Limited statutory elections exist for small/family SARLs under CGI Article 239 bis AA to be taxed in the name of partners; groups may elect tax consolidation under CGI Article 223 A. Hybrid mismatch rules under EU ATAD apply, but no broad pass-through election is available for a regular SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA) / Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 (domestic 'franchise en base' threshold for sales of goods). Non-established foreign suppliers generally have no turnover-based exemption and must register from the first taxable transaction; EU distance-selling thresholds of EUR 10,000 apply under the VAT OSS scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing for domestic B2B supplies is phased from 1 September 2026 for large/mid-sized enterprises and 1 September 2027 for smaller businesses, using certified Partner Dematerialisation Platforms (PDPs) transmitting structured invoices (Factur-X/UBL/CII) by API to DGFIP; B2C and cross-border flows require e-reporting to DGFIP. There is no physical stamping or continuous transaction clearance for VAT; Chorus Pro remains mandatory for public-sector invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies on proof that goods have physically left the customs territory of the EU under an electronic customs export declaration and that title/risk passed to a non-EU buyer. Offshore services may qualify when supplied to a non-EU taxable person or when directly and effectively connected with exported goods. The exporter must hold transport documents in its own name and provide evidence within the statutory retention period.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export VAT zero-rating is rigorously audited by DGFIP and French customs. If conditions are not met, VAT becomes due together with late interest (0.20% per month) and penalties of up to 40% for bad faith and 80% for fraud; fraudulent export schemes may also incur criminal penalties, loss of tax-representative relief, and joint liability for collection.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France); the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) within the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique is the competent foreign-exchange and foreign-investment administration authority; ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) supervises credit institutions and electronic money institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a euro-area Member State; the euro is fully convertible and France operates no exchange-control rationing on current-account or capital-account transactions. Current-account payments, trade settlements, service payments, and profit remittances are unrestricted under EU capital and payment movement rules. A French SARL may remit profits to non-resident shareholders after ordinary corporate formalities; such distributions may be subject to French dividend withholding tax at 30% by default or a lower rate under an applicable tax treaty, but no exchange-control authorization is required. Capital-account convertibility is likewise free: non-resident ownership of a French SARL, inbound capital contributions, shareholder loans, and repatriation of liquidation proceeds are permitted. France only imposes statistical balance-of-payments reporting to Banque de France for cross-border direct investment and, for narrowly defined sensitive sectors, prior review by the French Treasury; wholesale distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames is not a sensitive sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender or mandatory conversion requirements exist. France imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts received in foreign currency. Export proceeds may be retained in EUR or convertible foreign currency, reflected in the SARL's statutory accounts, and used for operational treasury purposes. Exporters only need to satisfy customs declaration rules, tax reporting, and, where a bank requests it, the underlying commercial documentation supporting the SWIFT credit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. via Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne networks

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate, institution-specific, and subject to legal constraints. An EU/EEA licensed electronic money institution can provide a payment or e-money account usable for platform-pay receipts and low-value disbursements, relying on the PSD2 passport into France. A UK or non-EEA offshore EMI does not benefit from EU passporting after Brexit and cannot provide the SARL with a French-classified account or a transparent domestic payment environment without a licensed EU partner bank. Such offshore EMIs should not be used as the primary treasury, capital escrow, commercial-LC, or FX-hedging platform. A French ACPR-regulated credit institution remains mandatory for the blocked capital deposit needed at company formation and for documentary trade finance and lawful access to bank-provided FX hedging.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML law and ACPR practice do not impose an absolute statutory requirement that every director appear physically at a branch before account opening. Remote opening is legally possible using certified identity verification, video KYC, and qualified electronic signatures. In practice, most first-tier French banks require at least one identification meeting with the gérant or a duly authorized representative, and many will accept a remote interview if the beneficial owner is located outside France. Non-resident directors should be prepared for a video interview, notarized and apostilled identity and corporate documents, a clear source-of-funds narrative, and the physical visit of a locally appointed agent or the completion of a bank-specific remote opening procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner with no French tax residence and no existing EEA banking relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport or secured national ID; proof of residential address; certified apostilled copies of identity documents; RBE beneficial-owner registration receipt; KBIS extract not older than three months; SARL bylaws and powers of attorney; bank reference from the shareholder's home-country institution; personal or corporate source-of-funds documentation; commercial explanation of the ophthalmic eyewear wholesale business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed SARL with limited local substance and an unusually large inbound capital transfer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized or certified statutory bylaws; bank capital deposit attestation; lease or premises agreement with an operational address in France; detailed business plan for frame distribution; supplier purchase orders or framework agreements; sales contracts or letters of intent from optician chains; projected cash-flow model; SIRET/SIREN tax registration; written confirmation that the received funds are exclusively used for commercial working capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to or from a supplier or shareholder located in a jurisdiction categorized as higher AML risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying international trade agreements for acetate eyeglass frames; supplier proforma and final commercial invoices; packing lists and bills of lading; Incoterms and customs entry documentation; proof of goods delivery; detailed payment purpose using trade nomenclature; corporate authorization by the SARL gérant; originator and beneficiary due-diligence data from the correspondent bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sole shareholder or gérant funding the company with personal savings or a third-party loan of unexplained origin.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Personal tax returns for the preceding two to three years; bank account statements showing salary, dividends, or accumulated liquid assets; source-of-wealth explanation; capital subscription deed; bank attestation of deposit of funds; the shareholder's passport and proof of address; declaration that the contribution is not financed by unverifiable third parties; where a loan is used, a written loan agreement and lender KYC profile.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a French SARL, cash capital must be deposited before company registration into a blocked account opened in the company name with a bank, a notary, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or Banque de France. The compliant wire protocol requires the non-resident shareholder to send a SWIFT MT103 to the blocked account with the beneficiary stated as the SARL in formation, the account reference of the blocked account, and an unambiguous remittance narrative such as 'Souscription et libération du capital social' and the future RCS/SIREN reference. The bank will verify the sending account, the identity of the shareholder, the source of funds, and the legal basis of the contribution. The banking purpose should be presented as an inbound direct-investment capital contribution, not as a trade payment or ambiguous personal transfer. Upon receipt, the bank issues a deposit certificate confirming the blocked funds; following publication/registration of the SARL, the funds are released to the operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For European Economic Area suppliers, the normal clearing rail is the SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR, which requires no SWIFT messaging. For suppliers in China, the United States, or other third countries, the recommended rail is a SWIFT MT103 over SWIFT gpi with full beneficiary bank identifiers, commercial invoice references, and the goods description 'ophthalmic eyewear frames'. For large-value or new-supplier transactions, a confirmed irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit issued subject to UCP600 through the SARL's French bank is the appropriate security-clearing rail; documentary collection with documents against payment may also be used. All outbound trade disbursements must be supported by the proforma invoice, purchase order, shipping documents, Incoterms, and the French customs import declaration reference, and the payment purpose should clearly reference the purchase of acetate eyewear frames from the named supplier.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot EUR/USD conversion with immediate settlement under the French bank's treasury master agreement
Outright EUR/USD forward FX contracts with firm tenors matched to confirmed trade payables or receivables
Flexible or date-optional EUR/USD forwards allowing early or delayed delivery to cover invoice timing uncertainty
EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF outright forwards where the SARL has real frame-purchase or distribution exposure in those currencies
EUR/CNH outright forwards for trade obligations invoiced in offshore renminbi
USD/CNH non-deliverable forward used strictly as a hedge against CNY-denominated procurement exposure
Plain vanilla European FX options purchased to cap adverse rate movement while preserving upside, with no speculative option-writing policy
Cross-currency swap between EUR and USD for long-dated supply commitments, matched to the underlying order book
Short-tenor FX swap or swap-to-next transactions for cash-flow rebalancing, limited to genuine liquidity-management operations

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax rate. A reduced 15% rate may apply to qualifying small companies on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to ownership, turnover and paid-in-capital conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: France generally permits indefinite carryforward of tax losses, subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000. Tax losses may generally be carried back to the immediately preceding financial year, limited to the lower of that year's profit and EUR 1,000,000. Research and development tax credits, innovation incentives and certain regional investment regimes may reduce the effective tax burden. No general statutory tax holiday applies to a standard wholesale eyewear SARL.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD and corporate tax package forms 2058-A-SD, 2058-B-SD, 2058-C-SD, 2058-E-SD, 2058-F-SD and 2058-G-SD, filed electronically through the professional account on impots.gouv.fr using the EFI or EDI procedure.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with separate installment and balance payment filings.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the corporate income tax return is generally due by the second business day following 1 May of the following year. For other year-ends, filing is generally due within three months after the end of the financial year. The tax balance is generally payable by the applicable statutory payment deadline, commonly the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN, registered office, tax office, financial-year opening and closing dates, and legal form.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SARL's French SIREN and registered office. Identify the foreign parent or shareholders only in the relevant ownership, related-party and withholding disclosures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss, applicable corporate tax rate, gross corporate income tax, credits, reductions, withholding tax credits and net tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute tax on the French SARL's separate taxable result. Do not consolidate foreign shareholder income unless a valid French tax consolidation regime applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss adjusted for non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, depreciation differences, provisions, financial expenses, foreign taxes and other permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude shareholder-level expenses unless incurred for the SARL's business and supported by arm's-length documentation. Apply French limitations to interest deductions, provisions and related-party charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year loss, prior-year losses used, remaining losses available for carryforward and any loss carryback claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Track losses at the French SARL level. A change in activity, merger, substantial change in business or abusive restructuring may restrict loss utilization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, reductions, foreign tax credits and other offsets against corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits legally attributable to the French SARL and retain supporting certificates, invoices, payroll records and foreign tax evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information concerning direct or indirect holdings, related entities, significant transactions and transactions with entities in non-cooperative jurisdictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign parent, sister companies, controlled entities, intra-group financing, management fees, royalties, goods purchases and sales, and any non-cooperative-jurisdiction connection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant transfer-pricing information, including the nature and amount of controlled transactions where disclosure thresholds or documentation requirements apply.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use consistent transaction categories, currencies, counterparties, contractual terms and pricing methods. Reconcile disclosed amounts to the general ledger and customs records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly corporate income tax installments, generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, subject to statutory exceptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate installments using the legally prescribed prior-year or current-year tax basis. Monitor the final installment adjustment and large-company surcharge rules where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax balance or refund after crediting installments and eligible tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to Form 2065, accounting tax provisions and payment records. A refund claim must be supported by the filed return and documentary evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding and social levies on dividends, interest, royalties and other distributions or investment income paid to recipients where French withholding applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File and pay when the SARL makes a reportable payment. Apply treaty or EU relief only after validating residence, beneficial ownership, eligibility and procedural evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing commonly triggers a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% after a formal notice and potentially 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abusive conduct. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month, subject to statutory adjustments and exceptions. Inaccurate returns may trigger tax reassessment, interest, penalties of 40% for deliberate failure and up to 80% for fraudulent conduct.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: French VAT return CA3 No. 3310-CA3-SD and related European VAT listings, filed electronically through the professional account on impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Monthly or quarterly depending on the VAT regime and prior-year VAT liability; annual summary may apply under specified simplified regimes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The electronic VAT return and payment are generally due on the date assigned to the taxpayer's professional tax account, commonly during the month following the reporting period. Intra-Community acquisition, dispatch and recapitulative filings have separate statutory deadlines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CA3, taxable turnover by VAT rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic taxable sales classified by applicable French VAT rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the correct place-of-supply rules to wholesale eyewear, including domestic sales, exports, intra-Community supplies and imports.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: VAT-exempt intra-Community supplies, exports and other zero-rated transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain transport evidence, valid customer VAT numbers, customs export records and commercial invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recoverable VAT on purchases, imports, logistics, professional services and overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify invoice formalities, business purpose, import VAT documentation and reverse-charge treatment for foreign suppliers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: VAT due and simultaneously deductible on qualifying cross-border services, acquisitions and imports.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply reverse charge where the French SARL is the liable customer and reconcile entries with supplier invoices and EU recapitulative statements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or payment may trigger a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest. VAT reassessments may carry 10%, 40% or 80% penalties depending on the conduct, with additional criminal exposure for organized or fraudulent VAT evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in France, and applicable tax treaties. A qualifying EU or EEA parent may obtain an exemption or refund subject to minimum ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, anti-abuse and beneficial-ownership conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify treaty entitlement, beneficial ownership, legal form, holding percentage, holding period and anti-abuse conditions, and collect any prescribed treaty forms or declarations. Apply the reduced rate at source only where French administrative conditions permit source relief; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and submit a refund claim to the French tax administration. File Form 2777-SD and pay the withholding and applicable social levies within the statutory deadline. Maintain shareholder registers, board resolutions, dividend vouchers, residence certificates and ownership evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Ordinary French-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to 25% withholding tax, subject to treaty limitations, EU interest-and-royalties relief where conditions are met, and special rules for non-cooperative jurisdictions. Interest paid by a French borrower to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but special rules may apply to payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, abusive arrangements and certain regulated instruments. Treaty royalty rates commonly range from 0% to 15%, and treaty interest rates commonly range from 0% to 15%, but the applicable bilateral treaty must be checked. Payments must reflect arm's-length terms and genuine beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 group or company turnover or gross assets generally triggers full French transfer-pricing documentation obligations, including a Master File and Local File, subject to statutory scope rules. Entities below the threshold may still be required to substantiate arm's-length pricing during an audit and may be subject to simplified documentation or information requests.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation regime. Substance is nevertheless required under French transfer-pricing rules, the abuse-of-law doctrine, beneficial-ownership principles, controlled-foreign-company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules and general anti-abuse provisions. The SARL should maintain real French commercial activity, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, inventory and logistics controls, decision-making evidence, premises where commercially appropriate, bank accounts, customer contracts and contemporaneous board and management records. A company with nominal activity, pass-through invoicing, circular cash flows or no decision-making capacity may face denial of deductions, withholding-tax relief, treaty benefits or tax residence claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of sales, fabricated invoices, false inventory, suppression of cash receipts, intentional misstatement of customs or VAT values, or knowingly false corporate tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, administrative penalties commonly up to 40% for deliberate conduct and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers, and criminal penalties that may include imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000. Aggravated cases may carry up to seven years' imprisonment and a fine of up to EUR 3,000,000, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and de facto directors may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, imprisonment, professional disqualification and civil liability. Under French tax law, a director may be held jointly liable for tax debt where serious and repeated misconduct made collection impossible. Travel restrictions are not automatic; judicial control, passport restrictions or travel bans may arise only under applicable criminal or procedural orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing-trader arrangements, fictitious intra-Community supplies, false VAT numbers, unjustified input-VAT recovery, duplicate invoices or deliberate misclassification of imports and exports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessment, repayment of improperly recovered VAT, surcharges generally ranging from 40% to 80%, late-payment interest, possible joint and several liability in specified cases, and criminal prosecution for aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly organize or approve VAT fraud may incur criminal fines, imprisonment, professional bans and personal tax liability. Directors cannot rely solely on accountant preparation where they approved or ignored manifestly fraudulent transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially low imports, inflated management fees or royalties, non-arm's-length financing, undocumented intercompany services, profit shifting to low-tax affiliates or inconsistent customs and tax valuations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment to taxable income, possible secondary adjustment or deemed distribution, withholding tax, late-payment interest, documentation penalties and a potential EUR 10,000 minimum penalty or a higher percentage-based penalty where statutory documentation failures apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SARL is normally the primary liable taxpayer. Directors may become personally exposed for deliberate tax fraud, serious management misconduct, insolvency-related asset dissipation or participation in a sham arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal French company without operational substance, conduit dividend or royalty flows, circular funding, nominee directors, back-to-back payments or treaty shopping designed principally to obtain withholding relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits or EU exemptions, withholding at domestic rates, reassessment under the abuse-of-law doctrine, interest, penalties of up to 80% in severe cases and potential criminal fraud exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil and criminal liability where they knowingly implement the arrangement. Corporate separateness is not a defense to personal participation in fraud, abuse of law or misappropriation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, failing to identify beneficial owners, using high-risk payment intermediaries, structuring transactions to avoid controls, or processing funds inconsistent with the eyewear wholesale business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious transaction reporting obligations, account freezing, confiscation, administrative sanctions, criminal prosecution, fines and imprisonment depending on the underlying offense. Professionals subject to AML supervision may also face regulator-imposed disciplinary measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may incur criminal liability for money laundering or participation in the predicate offense, including imprisonment, fines, confiscation and professional bans. Travel restrictions may be imposed by judicial order but are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Undervaluing acetate frames, misclassifying tariff codes, falsifying country of origin, evading import VAT or duties, or using incorrect importer-of-record information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of customs duties and import VAT, customs penalties, seizure or forfeiture of goods, suspension or loss of customs authorizations, and criminal sanctions for intentional customs fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company, customs declarant and responsible officers may be liable according to their roles. Directors may face personal criminal liability where they ordered, knowingly approved or concealed customs fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal profit distribution and insolvency misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring dividends without distributable profits, returning capital through disguised payments, continuing distributions while insolvent, preferring related creditors or transferring assets below value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restitution of unlawful distributions, director liability for insolvency deficiencies, annulment of suspect-period transactions, management bans, personal bankruptcy restrictions and criminal penalties where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be ordered to contribute to insolvency liabilities and may receive a prohibition on managing companies. Criminal exposure may arise for misuse of corporate assets, fraudulent bankruptcy or falsification of accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Accounting falsification and corporate records failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining incomplete books, backdating invoices, omitting liabilities, fabricating stock records, failing to retain supporting documents or presenting materially false annual accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, accounting penalties, rejection of deductions, civil damages and criminal penalties for falsification, misuse of company assets or presentation of inaccurate accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be personally prosecuted for approving or presenting false accounts and may face fines, imprisonment, management bans, civil restitution and liability in insolvency proceedings.
